open.thesis: 84% rostered nationally and dropped by Footballers — an ownership anomaly, not a bad player. Listed WR1 for Jacksonville ahead of Meyers.
open.falsifiedIf: Target share stays under about 18% through week 3, or Meyers/Washington pass him on the depth chart.
open.review: 14 Sep: wobbling. 7.0 in week 1. Reporting has Meyers and Parker Washington at the top of that room with Thomas and Hunter chasing, and PFN project a 19.3% target share. Not falsified, but the premise that he is the listed WR1 ahead of Meyers is now contested. Hold to week 3 as planned.

open.thesis: Pittsburgh's listed RB1 and the primary passing-down back. Chem switched to full PPR, which doubles the value of the receiving edge that had made him a sit.
open.falsifiedIf: Dowdle out-touches him materially two weeks running, or Warren's target share drops below Dowdle's.
open.review: 14 Sep: HELD. Warren out-touched Dowdle by five, outpaced him by two carries and one target, and ran 4.6 yards per carry to Dowdle's 1.9. PFN's 3:2-to-Dowdle model was wrong. ESPN expect Warren to stay the narrow leader into week 2 at New England.

open.thesis: Reconstructed after the fact from reporting, not from the run that made the add. Likely signed 3yr/$40M to follow Harbaugh from Baltimore and is the undisputed Giants TE1 and primary slot option, with Nabers coming off an ACL and a receiver room only four deep. 16.9 in week 1. The add was right.
open.falsifiedIf: Nabers returns to full health and Likely's route share drops below about 60%, or Theo Johnson takes the 11-personnel snaps back.
open.review: 14 Sep: a later run recommended dropping him for Xavier Worthy. That recommendation is withdrawn. Likely outscored Pitts 16.9 to 0.0 and has the better role; the Chem flex being RB/WR does not make a productive TE worthless, it makes him the TE1 in waiting.

open.thesis: 8 of 9 for 138 and two scores, led Carolina in every receiving category while McMillan was quiet until garbage time. 50% rostered is an anomaly in a ten-team league. Carolina draw Atlanta then Cleveland. Chem priority resets weekly so the claim is free.
open.falsifiedIf: McMillan reasserts as the clear alpha and Coker's target share falls under about 18% across weeks 2-3, or the week 1 line proves to have been garbage-time inflated.

closed.summary: One bench slot went Goedert -> Allgeier -> Likely in five days. Each step was defensible on projection; the sequence gained nothing and cost two roster moves. The Allgeier drop also came two days after he was named Arizona's listed RB1.

Recommended dropping Kyle Monangai for Tre Tucker on 13 Sep. Monangai returned from the knee and scored 20.4; Tucker's Bowers-vacuum thesis now has a return date on it. Not acted on. Screening a bench body on projection alone is what the strategy warns against.

A 13 Sep run recommended adding Xavier Worthy and dropping Isaiah Likely, on the reasoning that a second TE is structurally unplayable in a RB/WR flex. Likely scored 16.9 and Pitts scored 0.0. The structural argument was sound and the conclusion was still wrong, because it valued the slot rather than the player. Withdrawn.
